tasks.short: Read students' plan goals and curriculum goals, write lesson objectives per level, make visual objective cards, explain the objectives and check at the end whether they were reached.

steps.what: Special education teacher reads each student's plan goals and the curriculum goals
Special education teacher establishes clear objectives for lessons, units and projects per level group

loop.input: The lesson topic, the goal codes and the level groups of the class; no names or support needs.
loop.output: Draft objectives per level group, each tagged with a goal code.
loop.check: Code rejects objectives without a valid goal code; the teacher reads every objective against the goal's text and the level group and rewrites objectives whose meaning or level is off.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher writes them.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives must be phrased per level and topic; a fixed list is too coarse.

steps.what: Special education teacher makes visual objective cards for the board
Special education teacher communicates those objectives to students at the start of the lesson
Special education teacher checks with students whether the objective was reached

tasks.design: The student records system ({OTHER}) shows each student's plan goals next to the curriculum goals in the lesson planner. A bounded step drafts objectives per level group tagged with goal codes, from the topic and level groups only, and the teacher edits every objective. A template turns the objectives into pictogram cards for the board. Explaining and checking with students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Goals were looked up in separate plans and objectives written and drawn per lesson.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft objectives from goals, and templates make pictogram cards.
tasks.still_hard: Objectives for students with very different needs take the teacher's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Rephrasing an objective so an anxious student believes they can reach it.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafted objectives instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether templates free assistants for students.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference found.
Support needs in a student's plan are health data; no names or needs go into the drafting step.

assumptions: Boundary: from student plans to the end-of-lesson check; teaching the lesson is outside.
Input contract: plan goals in the student records system; goal codes from the national curriculum; fallback is writing by hand.
Explaining and checking do not change.
No pupil data go into the drafting step.
s2 keeps 70 because the teacher reads and rewrites every drafted objective.
research_questions: How much of each draft does the teacher keep?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits drafted objectives.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps level groups current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts are rarely usable for these level groups and many cards need own pictures, so s2 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 70 (16.5); high: drafts and the card template used as designed (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree behaviour goals with the student, practise behaviour through role play, praise and reward during the day, tally rewards and incidents and share the weekly graph with parents.

steps.what: Special education teacher agrees behaviour goals with the student
Special education teacher teaches socially acceptable behavior through role play and prompts
Special education teacher gives positive reinforcement with praise and tokens
Special education teacher tallies tokens and incidents: on a paper chart today, by tapping them on a tablet that builds the weekly graph after the change
Special education teacher checks the week's graph before it goes: counts match the day's records, the right student, wording fit for parents
Special education teacher sends the checked weekly graph to the parents: as a written note today, one send through the parent app after the change

tasks.design: The teacher taps tokens and incidents per behaviour goal on a tablet ({OTHER}), which builds the weekly graph instead of a paper chart. The teacher checks the week's graph and sends it once to the parents through the parent app. Agreeing goals, practising and reinforcing stay with the teacher; no system infers students' emotions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tallies were kept on paper and summarised by hand for parents.
tasks.enabler_now: Classroom apps record behaviour tallies and send summaries to parents.
tasks.still_hard: Tapping during a tense moment is not always possible.
tasks.human_edge: Catching a student doing well and saying so at the right moment.

reach.learn: Whether weekly graphs speed up plan reviews.

evidence.claim: Classroom apps record behaviour tallies and send weekly summaries to parents.
AI that infers pupils' emotions is banned in education.
Parents' and pupils' councils must consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student plan to parents informed; formal plan reviews are outside.
Input contract: behaviour goals agreed with the student and recorded by the teacher; fallback is the paper chart.
Agreeing, practising and reinforcing do not change.
No AI analyses behaviour.
Marking each token or incident is a first record and keeps its time; s4 keeps 70 because only adding up and drawing the weekly chart go. s5 keeps 25 for the send.
research_questions: Do parents follow up more at home?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; checking the graph is step s4b.

approvals.approved_version: The week's behaviour graph for this student exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the student's parents through the parent app; corrections need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tablet is often not at hand, so tallies stay partly on paper and s4 keeps 85 (5.2); high: tallies tapped on the tablet (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather marks, notes and incidents, arrange meeting times, confer with parents, colleagues and counselors, record agreements and follow them up.

steps.what: Special education teacher gathers marks, notes and incidents before the meeting
Parents agree a meeting time: by e-mail today, by picking a slot in the parent app after the change
Special education teacher arranges meeting times with parents and colleagues by e-mail
Special education teacher confers with parents, counselors and administrators to resolve students' problems
Special education teacher records the agreements in the student's file
Special education teacher follows up the agreements with those involved

tasks.design: A student overview in the records system ({OTHER}) shows marks, notes and incidents for the last period on one page. Parents book a meeting slot in the parent app, and agreements go into a short form with an owner and a date per agreement. Conferring and following up stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was gathered from several screens and times agreed by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Records systems show student overviews, and parent apps take bookings.
tasks.still_hard: Problems that span home and school need long conversations.
tasks.human_edge: Finding common ground with parents who feel blamed.

reach.learn: Whether agreements with owners get followed up.

evidence.claim: Student records systems show overviews of marks, notes and incidents, and parent apps take bookings.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff; parents and pupils to pupil-data rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from a concern to followed-up agreements; formal referrals are outside.
Input contract: marks and notes in the records system; slots set by the teacher; fallback is e-mail.
Conferring and following up do not change.
Parents' slot picking is shown in s6 at share 1 and priced as customer time; colleagues' time is outside the teacher's savings. s2 keeps 40 for setting slots and agreeing times with colleagues.
Recording agreements is a first record: s4 keeps 85, saving only the layout and the owner and date fields.
research_questions: Are agreements followed up on time?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads the student overview.

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; setting open slots is part of s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: notes sit partly outside the records system and few parents book in the app, so s1 keeps 60 and s2 keeps 70 (14.8); high: overview and app used as designed (23.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read specialists' reports, choose strategies, adapt materials to each student's needs, write the strategies into the student's plan and try them in class.

steps.what: Special education teacher reads reports from psychologists and therapists

loop.input: Specialist reports in the student's file, inside the school's contracted environment.
loop.output: A list of stated needs and advised adaptations, each with the report and page it comes from.
loop.check: Code rejects items without a source page and diagnostic labels the reports do not state; the teacher reads each listed need against the cited page and reads the full report where an item is unclear.
loop.stop: One pass per report set; unclear reports are read in full by the teacher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports are long free text from different specialists.

steps.what: Special education teacher develops strategies to meet the needs of students with a variety of handicapping conditions
Special education teacher adapts materials with larger print, simpler text and pictograms

loop.input: Lesson text and the target reading level; no student data.
loop.output: The text rewritten at the target level, with pictogram suggestions.
loop.check: Code measures the reading level of the result; the teacher reads every adapted text against the original to check the content and tasks are unchanged before use.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher adapts it by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting text at another level needs free text; fixed rules cannot do it.

steps.what: Special education teacher writes the strategies into the student's plan
Special education teacher implements the strategies in class and adjusts them

tasks.design: A bounded step lists needs and advised adaptations from specialist reports with the page each comes from, inside the school's contracted environment, and the teacher reads every item. A lesson editor rewrites texts at the target reading level with pictogram suggestions, and the teacher checks each text. The student plan module in the records system ({OTHER}) holds strategies in structured fields with review dates. Choosing and trying strategies stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were read in full and materials adapted by hand for each student.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors rewrite text at another level, and models can list points from long reports with sources.
tasks.still_hard: Reports may conflict; choosing a strategy is the teacher's call.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which adaptation a student will accept without feeling singled out.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks listed needs and adapted texts instead of producing them.

reach.learn: Whether structured plans speed up yearly reviews.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
Support needs in a student's plan are health data; a DPIA is needed for new pupil-data systems.
AI that sets a pupil's education level is high-risk; this design does not.

assumptions: Boundary: from specialist reports to strategies tried; formal plan meetings are outside.
Input contract: reports from specialists in the student's file; reading levels set by the school; fallback is reading and adapting by hand.
Choosing and trying strategies do not change.
Reports stay inside the school's contracted environment.

s1 keeps 60 because the teacher checks each listed need against the report; s3 keeps 55 because every adapted text is read against the original; s4 keeps 70 because the strategies are still written by the teacher, only the fields and review dates are set.
research_questions: Do adapted materials reach students sooner?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads the listed needs.
Special education teacher checks adapted texts.

incremental.description: Special education teacher reports wrong listings to the support coordinator.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: reports are short or unclear so the teacher reads them in full, and few texts are adapted, so s1 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 85 (11.2); high: listings and the lesson editor used as designed (22.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps teaching, behaviour work, conversations and choices of strategy; looking up goals, paper charts and adapting texts by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted objectives and adapted texts
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time one to one with the students who need it most.
